info.title: Orch8.io API
info.description:
Durable task sequencing engine — REST API.

All versioned endpoints are available under the `/api/v1` prefix (canonical) and also at the bare path for backward compatibility. Bare-path responses carry Deprecation, Sunset, and successor-version +            Link headers. Health and metrics endpoints remain at the root +            (`/health/*`, `/metrics`).

Readiness probe: returns 200 only if the database is reachable AND the
engine tick loop is still running. A dead scheduler with a live DB must not
report ready — otherwise the LB keeps routing to a server that accepts work
but never executes it.

Deployment info for UI chrome: engine version plus the optional
operator-set environment label/color (`ORCH8_ENV_LABEL`,
`ORCH8_ENV_COLOR`). Read straight from the environment — this is
cosmetic metadata, not engine configuration, so it does not flow
through `EngineConfig`.

post.summary: DLQ surgery: re-run an instance from an arbitrary block.
post.description:
Wipes the target block's outputs and the outputs of every block at or
after it in the sequence's top-level `blocks` array (including blocks
nested inside wiped composites), optionally shallow-merges a context
patch into `context.data`, and re-schedules the instance immediately.
Earlier blocks keep their outputs: on the flat all-step execution path
the completed-blocks check skips them, so side-effectful handlers do not
run twice. On the tree path the execution tree is rebuilt from scratch —
the exact same semantics as `POST /instances/{id}/retry`, which also
deletes the tree while preserving real outputs.

Linear assumption: "after" is defined by position in the top-level
`blocks` array, which is the order both execution paths (flat fast path
and tree evaluator) run top-level blocks in. The target must itself be a
top-level block — resuming from a block nested inside a composite is not
supported.

200.description: Instance re-scheduled from the given block

400.description: Unknown block, or instance is in a state that cannot be resumed

ABSplitDef.description:
A/B split: deterministically route each instance to one of several
weighted variants. The chosen variant is persisted in the block output
so re-executions always follow the same path.

ABVariant.description: One arm of an A/B split.

blocks.description: Blocks to execute when this variant is chosen.

ApiCapability.description: Coarse principal capabilities enforced before tenant API routing.

acknowledge_side_effect_risk.description: Required for recipes which may repeat an external side effect.

ArtifactRef.description:
A durable reference to stored bytes. Travels in step outputs / context as
`{ "artifact": { ... } }` — never the bytes themselves.

content_type.description: MIME type captured at store time (e.g. `image/png`, `text/html`).

id.description: Opaque artifact id (unique within the instance).

instance_id.description:
Owning instance — artifacts are instance-scoped (object keys are
prefixed with it, so an instance's blobs can be enumerated via
`list_artifacts` and removed via `delete_artifact`). Note: unlike DB
rows, object-store blobs are not yet swept automatically on instance
deletion — that cleanup is a follow-up.

AuditLogEntry.description: An immutable audit log entry recording a state transition or lifecycle event.

block_id.description: Block ID related to this event, if any.

details.description: Additional event data (e.g., error message, signal payload).

BatchAction.description: The operation a batch action applies to every matched instance.

dry_run.description: When true, count matching instances and apply nothing.

limit.description: Hard cap on how many instances are acted on. Default 1000, max 10000.

signal_type.description:
Custom signal name for the `signal` action (no `custom:` prefix). Ignored
for the other actions.

applied.description: Instances the action was successfully applied to.

failed.description: Instances where applying the action errored.

matched.description: Instances matched by the filter (capped by `limit`).

skipped.description:
Instances the action did not apply to (e.g. retry of a non-Failed
instance, or a signal to a terminal instance).

events.description:
Events read from a transactional outbox. Retries are safe because each
item carries its producer idempotency identity.

allOf.description: Invoke another sequence as a sub-workflow.

oneOf.description: Invoke another sequence as a sub-workflow.

allOf.description: A/B split: route traffic to one of several variants by weight.

oneOf.description: A/B split: route traffic to one of several variants by weight.

allOf.description:
Cancellation scope: child blocks cannot be cancelled by external cancel signals.
Provides subtree-level non-cancellability (Temporal-style structured concurrency).

oneOf.description:
Cancellation scope: child blocks cannot be cancelled by external cancel signals.
Provides subtree-level non-cancellability (Temporal-style structured concurrency).

allOf.description:
Saga: sequential steps with compensating actions, rolled back in
reverse order if any step's action fails.

oneOf.description:
Saga: sequential steps with compensating actions, rolled back in
reverse order if any step's action fails.

BlockDefinition.description:
A block is either a leaf (step) or a composite (parallel, race, etc.).

This recursive enum IS the workflow DSL.
Each variant wraps its definition in `Box<T>` so the enum itself stays a
single word. `StepDef` is large (14 fields with many `Option<...>`), and
without boxing every `BlockDefinition` — even `SubSequence`, which is small
— paid the full size. `Box<T>` is transparent to both `serde` (the default
impl delegates to the inner type so wire format is unchanged) and `utoipa`
(which forwards `ToSchema` through `Box<T>`), so this is an internal
representation change only.

output_ref.description: Reference key if output was externalized (exceeded size threshold).

BlockOutputSummary.description:
Summary of one recorded output — the payload itself stays behind the
lazy detail endpoint (`/instances/{id}/outputs`).

Budget.description:
Optional per-instance resource budget enforced by the scheduler.

When any configured limit is exceeded (recorded LLM token usage or
executed step count), the scheduler pauses the instance with
`metadata.paused_reason = "budget_exceeded"` instead of letting it keep
spending. Resume via the normal `Paused -> Scheduled` transition.

v1 semantics: the budget is checked when the scheduler claims the
instance, *before* executing work for that tick. A resumed instance
therefore gets one more tick of work before the check fires again; if the
budget is still exceeded it pauses again on the next claim. A single
tick's work may also overshoot the limit slightly (the check is
pre-flight, not mid-step).

max_attention_units.description: Maximum human-attention units reserved by the execution.

max_bytes_transferred.description: Maximum bytes transferred across runtime boundaries.

max_cost_microunits.description: Maximum monetary spend in millionths of the configured currency unit.

max_energy_millijoules.description: Maximum estimated energy consumption in millijoules.

max_external_calls.description: Maximum number of calls crossing an external-effect boundary.

max_input_tokens.description: Max total LLM input (prompt) tokens recorded for this instance.

max_output_tokens.description: Max total LLM output (completion) tokens recorded for this instance.

max_total_tokens.description: Max combined (input + output) LLM tokens recorded for this instance.

max_wall_time_ms.description: Maximum elapsed execution time in milliseconds.

metadata.description:
Top-level `metadata` equality filters (key → value), combined with AND.
Served by the same indexed path as `GET /instances?metadata.k=v`.

offset_secs.description: Shift `next_fire_at` by this many seconds (positive = later, negative = earlier).

percent.description: Percentage of new instances routed to the candidate (1–100).

CancellationScopeDef.description:
Cancellation scope: wraps child blocks in a non-cancellable boundary.

When a cancel signal is received, blocks inside a `CancellationScope`
continue executing until completion. The cancel takes effect only after
all scoped blocks finish.

CapsuleRequirements.description: Requirements that must be satisfied before accepting a capsule.

ChangeCursor.description:
Exclusive position in the tenant audit feed. Ordering is total even when
multiple changes share a timestamp because UUID is the tie-breaker.

Checkpoint.description: A checkpoint captures execution state at a point in time for efficient recovery.

checkpoint_data.description: Snapshot of execution state: completed block IDs, context, etc.

CircuitBreakerState.description:
Circuit breaker state for a (tenant, handler) pair.

Breakers are scoped per-tenant so a noisy customer cannot trip the circuit
for an unrelated tenant sharing the same handler name.

cooldown_secs.description: Cooldown period in seconds before transitioning from Open to `HalfOpen`.

failure_threshold.description: Threshold of failures before opening the circuit.

opened_at.description: When the circuit was last opened (to compute cooldown expiry).

tenant_id.description: Owning tenant — breakers are isolated per-tenant.

ClusterNode.description: Represents a running engine node in a multi-node cluster.

capabilities_withdrawn.description: New placement/claim capability was withdrawn before shutdown.

drain.description: If true, the node should stop accepting new work and drain.

execution_handoff_evidence.description: Durable evidence written only after the local scheduler has drained.

name.description: Human-readable node name (e.g. hostname or pod name).

CommercialContinuityPlan.description: Enforceable plan for hosted relay, Conformance Cloud, and OEM deployments.

CompiledPlacementPolicy.description: Human-editable placement policy compiled into the durable core vocabulary.

logs.description: Optional log lines the worker captured while running this task.

Confidence.description:
How confident the producer of a finding is in its diagnosis.

Diagnosis surfaces must never claim certainty while multiple
explanations remain possible — pick the honest level.

ContextAccess.description:
Controls which context sections a step handler can see.
When set, only the listed sections are passed to the handler.

`data` supports field-level granularity via [`FieldAccess`]; other sections
are all-or-nothing because they are small by design (`config`, `runtime`)
or append-only streams (`audit`).

data.description:
Controls read access to `context.data`. Accepts legacy `true`/`false`,
the keywords `"all"`/`"none"`, or an explicit `{"fields": [..]}` list.

value.description: Raw secret value (typically JSON) — will be stored and redacted on read.

overlap_policy.description:
Behavior when a fire is due while a previous run is still active:
`allow` (default), `skip`, `buffer_one`, `cancel_previous`.

oneOf.description:
Optional resource budget (token/step caps) enforced by the scheduler.
When any configured limit is exceeded the instance is paused with
`metadata.paused_reason = "budget_exceeded"`. Default: no budget.

dry_run.description:
Run this instance in dry-run mode: side-effecting steps (HTTP/LLM/MCP
calls, agent loops, event/signal emission, memory writes, block
injection, external plugins) skip their real effect and return a stub;
control flow and templating run normally. Any sequence can be run dry.
Default false.

dry_run_auto_approve.description:
When dry-run is on, auto-approve `human_review` gates with the default
choice so the simulation flows past them instead of pausing. Ignored
unless `dry_run` is true. Default false.

CredentialKind.description: The kind of secret held in a credential.

CredentialResponse.description:
API response for credentials — secret material is completely stripped.

Credential values never leave the server; they are only resolved
internally by step handlers (LLM, HTTP, etc.) via `credentials://<id>`.

enabled.description: Whether this credential can be resolved by step handlers.

has_refresh_token.description: Whether a refresh token is configured (true/false, never the value).

CronSchedule.description: A cron schedule that periodically creates instances of a sequence.

last_skipped_at.description: When the `skip` overlap policy last skipped an occurrence.

metadata.description: Extra metadata to inject into created instances.

overlap_policy.description: Behavior when a fire is due while a previous run is still active.

skipped_fires.description: Occurrences skipped by the `skip` overlap policy.

DebugTemplateRequest.description: Request body for the lightweight template debugger.

template.description: Raw template string to resolve (e.g. `"{{ context.data.name | upper }}"`).

error.description:
Top-level error when the template string is malformed or resolution
fails entirely.

result.description:
The resolved value after template evaluation, redacted.
`None` when the entire resolution failed.

result_type.description: JSON type of the resolved value (`string`, `number`, ...).

fire_at_local.description:
Fire at a specific local wall-clock time (ISO 8601 `NaiveDateTime`,
e.g. `"2026-03-08T02:30:00"`). When set, `duration` is ignored and
the engine converts this local time to UTC using the step-level
`timezone` (or the instance timezone as fallback). DST transitions
are handled by rolling forward to the next valid local time.

holidays.description:
Holiday dates (YYYY-MM-DD) to skip when `business_days_only` is true.
Merged with `context.config.holidays` at runtime for tenant-level calendars.

timezone.description:
Timezone for `fire_at_local` (IANA, e.g. `"America/New_York"`).
Falls back to the instance's timezone if omitted.

DeliveryErrorClass.description:
Normalized failure class for a delivery attempt. Metrics are emitted
by class (bounded cardinality), never by endpoint.

allOf.description:
The explanation itself: code, summary, evidence, remediations,
confidence.

DiagnosisCategory.description:
How strongly the evidence points at this explanation. Used as the
primary ranking key.

DiagnosisHealth.description: Whether the observed situation is normal, degraded, or self-contradictory.

DiffEntry.description: One semantic difference between two sequence versions.

DiffSeverity.description: How much a semantic-diff change matters, ordered.

DispatchMode.description: How tasks on a queue reach workers.

DlqGroup.description: One root-cause group of failed instances.

components.description:
The fingerprint's components — the grouping is explainable, never
a black box.

error_code.description:
Stable error code shared by the group (`HTTP_STATUS`, `TIMEOUT`,
`unknown`, ...).

sample_instance_ids.description: Up to ten newest instance ids for drill-down / sample retry.

force.description: Bulk only: explicit override when no successful sample exists.

limit.description:
Bulk only: cap on instances retried in this call (default 100,
max 500).

sample_verified_instance_id.description:
Bulk only: an instance from this group whose *sample retry*
succeeded (now `completed`). Verified server-side.

skipped.description: Instances skipped (no longer failed / no longer in the group).

EffectKind.description: Classification of a potentially externally visible operation.

EffectState.description: Evidence state for an external effect; this never claims exactly-once.

ErrorClass.description:
Broad, stable classification of where a failure originates. Used to
separate "fix your workflow" from "fix your infrastructure" without
reading messages.

EscalationDef.description: Action to take when an SLA deadline is breached.

handler.description: Handler name to invoke on breach (e.g. `"notify_slack"`, `"send_alert"`).

params.description: Parameters passed to the escalation handler.

auto_rolled_back.description: Applied automatically when a gate fails during canary.

EventEnvelope.description:
One ingested event. Canonical identity is
`(tenant_id, event_name, producer_event_id)` — re-sending the same
producer id is a safe no-op.

consumed_by.description: The instance whose wait consumed this event.

correlation_key.description: Tenant-scoped business correlation key (order id, customer id...).

producer_event_id.description: The producer's idempotency identity for this event.

event_names.description: Event names this wait listens for.

matched_event_ids.description: Envelope ids consumed by this wait so far.

matched_names.description: Names of events matched so far (deduplicated).

Evidence.description:
One piece of evidence backing a finding: a fact, where it was observed,
and when.

data.description: Optional structured payload (already redacted by the producer).

observed_at.description: When this fact was observed (not when the finding was assembled).

ExecutionContext.description: Multi-section execution context with different permission semantics.

runtime.description: Engine-managed runtime state. Read-only to step handlers.

ExecutionEpoch.description: Monotonic ownership generation for one portable execution.

events_truncated.description: True when `events` was truncated at the requested limit.

nodes.description: Definition tree nodes with their execution state.

share_path.description: Shareable deep-link path (ids only, never payloads).

logs.description: Optional log lines the worker captured while running this task.

FailureEnvelope.description:
Structured description of one failure, preserved alongside the
human-readable message.

block_id.description: Block that failed, when the failure is block-scoped.

error_code.description:
Stable machine code, `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`, e.g. `HANDLER_TIMEOUT`,
`HTTP_STATUS`, `NO_COMPATIBLE_WORKER`. Codes are producer-defined
but must be stable across releases.

external_status.description:
Normalized external status (HTTP status, DB SQLSTATE class, exit
code), when the failure came from an external dependency.

message.description:
The human-readable message. Kept verbatim; never used as the
primary machine interface.

oneOf.description:
The credential / queue / worker / plugin / breaker involved, when
applicable. This is an identifier, never a secret.

retryable.description: Whether the engine considered this retryable at the time.

FailureFingerprint.description: A stable, explainable root-cause fingerprint for grouping DLQ entries.

components.description:
The components that went into the hash, in order — kept so the
grouping is explainable, never a black box.

hash.description: Hex-encoded 64-bit FNV-1a hash of the normalized components.

Finding.description:
One read-only diagnostic statement with its evidence and suggested
remediations.

FindingSeverity.description: How severe a finding is for the operator.

retain_iterations.description:
Keep only the most recent N iterations' body-step outputs; older outputs
are compacted at each iteration boundary. `None` retains everything.

copied_blocks.description: Blocks whose recorded outputs would be copied into the fork.

re_executed_blocks.description: Blocks that would execute again in the fork.

sandbox_default.description: Forks start in dry-run (sandbox) mode unless explicitly overridden.

side_effect_blocks.description:
Re-executed blocks with external side effects — the UI must
require explicit confirmation for these.

ForkRequest.description:
Body for `POST /instances/{id}/fork`. `from_block_id` must be a top-level
block of the source's sequence; `context` (optional) is shallow-merged
into the fork's `context.data` with the same per-key semantics as
resume-from; `dry_run` defaults to **true** so a forked production
workflow does not re-fire side effects unless explicitly asked to.
`signals` are enqueued on the fork before it becomes claimable.

copied_blocks.description:
Number of pre-fork top-level blocks whose outputs were copied (the
fork will NOT re-execute these).

dry_run.description: Whether the fork runs in dry-run mode.

id.description: ID of the newly created fork.

rerun_blocks.description:
Pre-fork top-level blocks whose outputs could not be copied (never
executed, artifact-backed, or mid-flight sentinel) — these WILL
(re-)execute on the fork, in addition to everything from
`from_block_id` onward.

GateMetric.description: Gate metrics evaluated over canary observations.

GatewayManifest.description: Drop-in wrapper/gateway manifest used by `orch8 wrap`, MCP, and local workers.

GeneratedDataflowTypes.description: Deterministic language bindings and their canonical source schema.

HandlerCatalog.description: Catalog of every handler name the engine can serve.

builtin.description: Handlers executed in-process by the engine.

external.description: Handler names served by external workers (from the worker registry).

HumanChoice.description: One option presented to the human reviewer in advanced mode.

label.description: Display text shown in the UI.

value.description: Stable identifier stored in context and used for router matching.

allow_comment.description: When true, the reviewer can attach a free-text comment to their decision.

choices.description:
Choices the human can pick from. If `None`, the engine applies the
default yes/no preset.

escalation_handler.description:
If set and timeout expires, send a signal to this escalation target
instead of failing the step.

prompt.description: Prompt or instructions for the human reviewer.

store_as.description:
Context-variable name under which the picked value is stored
(`context.data[store_as]`). If `None`, the block id is used.

timeout.description:
Timeout in milliseconds before the step fails or escalates.
If omitted, waits indefinitely.

InFlightPolicy.description: How in-flight instances are treated when a release promotes.

producer_event_id.description:
Producer idempotency identity — re-sending the same id is a safe
no-op.

duplicate.description: True when the producer id was already known — nothing changed.

matched_wait.description: The wait (if any) this event was matched into.

satisfied.description:
True when the match satisfied the wait's join and resumed the
waiting instance.

blocks.description: Blocks must be a valid JSON array of `BlockDefinition` objects.

position.description: Position to inject at (0-indexed). If omitted, blocks are appended.

InjectedSignal.description:
A signal enqueued atomically with a resume-from or fork, so it is already
pending when the instance becomes claimable. Closes the race window of the
separate "reset, then signal" two-call pattern.

InspectTemplateRequest.description:
Request body for draft inspection: a definition (or stored sequence
id), the block to inspect, and the context/outputs fixture to resolve
against.

block_id.description: The step block whose params to inspect.

oneOf.description:
Draft sequence definition. Exactly one of `sequence` /
`sequence_id` must be set.

InstanceDiagnosisReport.description: The full report for one instance.

diagnoses.description:
Ranked: direct evidence first, then probable causes, then health
warnings; higher confidence first within a category.

state.description: Instance state at diagnosis time (engine state name).

InstanceId.description:
Newtype wrappers prevent mixing up UUIDs at compile time.
Zero cost at runtime (transparent newtypes).

InstanceState.description:
Instance states form a strict state machine.
Transitions are validated at runtime via `can_transition_to`.

InterceptorAction.description: An interceptor action that fires at a lifecycle point.

handler.description: Handler name to invoke (must be registered or dispatched to external worker).

params.description: Static params passed to the handler.

InterceptorDef.description:
Defines lifecycle hooks attached to a sequence.
Interceptors are evaluated at defined points in the instance lifecycle.

oneOf.description: Called after each step completes (success or failure).
Called before each step executes. Can modify context or skip the step.
Called when the instance completes.
Called when the instance fails.
Called when a signal is received.
Resume on the first matching event.
Resume once every named event has arrived (in any order).
Resume once `count` matching events arrived.

allowed_runtime_ids.description:
An empty list means any runtime. A non-empty list supports policies such
as "PII stays on this device" without embedding executable code.

poll_interval.description: Seconds to wait between loop-condition polls.

retain_iterations.description:
Keep only the most recent N iterations' body-step outputs; older outputs
are compacted (deleted) at each iteration boundary to bound storage
growth on long-running loops. `None` retains everything (default).

MigrateInstanceRequest.description:
Hot migration: rebind a running instance to a different sequence version.
The instance will pick up the new version's block definitions on its next tick.
Only non-terminal instances can be migrated.

target_sequence_id.description: The new sequence version to bind the instance to.

OverlapPolicy.description:
What to do when a schedule fires while a previous run it created is
still active (scheduled / running / waiting / paused).

oneOf.description:
Short-lived, fail-closed capability advertisement used for atomic
hardware, region, browser/mobile UI, network, and trust matching.

version.description: Optional worker build/deploy version, recorded on the worker registry.

PoolResource.description: A single resource within a pool.

daily_usage_date.description: Date of the current daily usage counter.

enabled.description: Whether this resource is active and available for assignment.

warmup_days.description: Number of days for the warmup ramp (0 = no warmup).

warmup_start.description: Date when this resource was added to the pool.

warmup_start_cap.description: Starting daily cap during warmup (ramps linearly to `daily_cap`).

weight.description: Weight for weighted rotation (higher = more assignments). Default 1.

PortableWorkOffer.description: Framework-neutral unit of work offered to capability-aware runtimes.

PreflightCheck.description: One named readiness check with its findings.

findings.description: Detailed findings (empty for a clean pass).

PreflightReport.description: The combined preflight report for one sequence.

PreflightStatus.description:
Outcome of a single preflight check.

Ordering is by increasing severity for aggregation: `Pass < Warning <
Unknown < Fail`. `Unknown` outranks `Warning` because unproven
readiness is riskier than a known cosmetic issue.

force.description: Promote even when gates are inconclusive or failing.

keep.description: Number of most recent checkpoints to keep.

push_url.description: Target URL for `push` mode (required when `mode = push`).

version.description: Optional worker build/deploy version, recorded on the worker registry.

handler_name.description: The handler name this rule applies to.

match_queue.description:
When set, the rule only applies if the task's currently-declared queue
equals this value (queue remap). `None` matches any current queue.

priority.description: Higher priority rules are evaluated first; the first match wins.

queue_override.description: The queue the matching task is routed to instead.

RedeliverPreview.description:
What a redelivery *would* send, without sending it. Secrets never
appear: the signature is described, not exposed.

last_error.description: The last error seen before parking.

previous_attempts.description: How many attempts were made before parking.

previous_delivery_id.description: Attempt history of the pass that parked this entry, if linked.

will_be_signed.description:
Whether the request will carry `X-Orch8-Timestamp` /
`X-Orch8-Signature` HMAC headers.

delivery_id.description:
The new attempt group recorded for this redelivery pass — inspect
it via `GET /webhooks/deliveries/{delivery_id}`.

redelivered.description: Whether the redelivery succeeded (and the outbox row was removed).

ReleaseDecision.description: Immutable audit record of one state transition (or attempted one).

ReleaseGate.description:
One release gate: the candidate may regress at most
`max_regression` (absolute difference, e.g. `0.05` = five
percentage points) versus the baseline, evaluated only once both
variants have at least `min_sample` terminal observations.

max_regression.description:
Maximum allowed absolute regression of the candidate vs. the
baseline (candidate − baseline).

min_sample.description:
Minimum terminal instances per variant before the gate is
conclusive.

Remediation.description:
A suggested, separately authorized action. Describing a remediation
never performs it.

oneOf.description:
Machine-applicable classification of the action, when the producer
knows it. Consumers must use this typed field instead of parsing
`command` strings; `None` means the action is manual.

command.description: Optional CLI command the operator can run verbatim.

link.description: Optional API route or dashboard path for the action.

side_effect_risk.description:
True when performing this action may repeat external side effects
(re-running a block, redelivering a webhook). UIs must require
explicit confirmation for these.

RemediationAction.description: Machine-applicable subset of a human remediation suggestion.

RemediationPreview.description: Stable preview generated from the current diagnosis and instance state.

coerced_to_string.description:
True when a non-string value was coerced into a string because the
expression sits inside a larger interpolated string.

expression.description: The original template expression (inner text of `{{ ... }}`).

fallback_used.description: True when the value came from a fallback segment, not the first.

param_path.description:
Dotted location of the parameter inside the block's `params`
(e.g. `body.email`, `headers.0.value`).

result_type.description: JSON type of the resolved value (`string`, `number`, ...).

source.description:
The fallback-chain segment that supplied the value (a source path
like `context.data.email`, or `literal` for a quoted default).

value.description: The resolved value, redacted. Absent for `missing` / `error`.

ResolutionStatus.description: Outcome of resolving one template expression.

ResolutionTrace.description: The full trace for one block's parameters.

entries.description: One entry per template expression found in the params.

resolved_params.description:
The block's params with every template resolved, redacted. `None`
when whole-params resolution failed (see `entries` for the error).

ResourceKey.description: Resource key for rate limiting, e.g. "mailbox:john@acme.com"

ResourcePool.description: A pool of resources that can be assigned to instances.

round_robin_index.description: Tracks the next index for round-robin rotation.

ResourceRef.description:
A reference to the resource a finding is about, precise enough for the
dashboard/CLI to deep-link to it.

id.description:
The resource identifier (UUID or name, whichever is canonical for
the kind).

name.description: Optional human-readable name when the id alone is opaque.

ResumeFromRequest.description:
Body for `POST /instances/{id}/resume-from/{block_id}`. The whole body is
optional; when present, `context` must be a JSON object whose top-level
keys are shallow-merged into `context.data` (same per-key semantics as
`StorageBackend::merge_context_data`) before the instance is re-scheduled.
`signals` are enqueued before the wake transition — they are pending by
the time the instance can run again.

RotationStrategy.description: Rotation strategy for assigning resources from a pool.

only_left.description: Blocks executed only by the left run, in execution order.

only_right.description: Blocks executed only by the right run, in execution order.

RuntimeCapabilities.description: Bounded facts used by compatibility and placement decisions.

capsule_signing_public_key.description: Base64 Ed25519 key authorized to sign capsules emitted by this runtime.

oneOf.description:
Current connectivity is deliberately distinct from offline capability:
a device may support offline execution while presently using Wi-Fi.

credentials.description:
Tenant-local credential references available to this runtime. Values
identify configured bindings, never secret material.

draining.description:
Draining runtimes remain discoverable for evidence but cannot receive
new work.

RuntimeConnectivity.description: Current network path reported by a runtime for bounded locality decisions.

current_step_started_at.description:
When the current step began executing. Used as the baseline for
per-step SLA deadlines and `wait_for_input` timeouts so earlier
steps do not eat into the timeout budget of later ones.

dry_run.description:
Dry-run mode. When `true`, side-effecting step handlers (`tool_call`,
`llm`, `mcp`, `agent`, `emit_event`, `send_signal`, `memory`,
`self_modify`, external plugins) skip their real effect and return a
stub output tagged `"dry_run": true`; control flow, templating and
branching still execute normally. Set once at instance creation and
propagated to child instances (e.g. sub-sequences). Engine-managed and
read-only to handlers — read it via `StepContext::is_dry_run`.

dry_run_auto_approve.description:
When dry-run is active, auto-resolve `human_review` / `wait_for_input`
gates with the default (first) choice instead of pausing, so the
simulation flows through human gates and exercises post-gate steps.
Ignored outside dry-run. Engine-managed.

run_id.description:
Identifies one *run* of the instance (string UUID v7). Stamped on the
first execution and regenerated by retry / resume-from-block /
DLQ-retry — which also reset `total_steps_executed`, `current_step`
and `started_at` — so a resurrected instance's webhooks are
distinguishable from the previous run's and the step counter does not
phantom-re-fail against `max_steps_per_instance`.

total_steps_executed.description:
Total number of step executions for this instance (including retries).
Used by mobile SDK to enforce `max_steps_per_instance`.

RuntimeKind.description: Physical class of a runtime eligible to own or execute work.

RuntimeTrustLevel.description: How strongly a runtime's identity and environment are verified.

SagaDef.description:
A saga: a sequence of steps that each carry an optional compensating
action. If any step's action fails, the compensations for every
already-completed step run in reverse order (LIFO) — the classic saga
pattern for distributed transactions without two-phase commit.

Compensation failures are recorded but do not stop the rollback: every
completed step's compensation gets a chance to run, best-effort. The
saga node itself always fails once compensation finishes (whether or
not every compensation succeeded) — the original action failure is
never silently absorbed.

action.description: The forward action for this saga step.

oneOf.description:
Compensating action run (in reverse order across all completed
steps) if a later step's action fails. `None` means this step has
no compensation — it is skipped during rollback.

candidate_lint.description:
Lint findings on the candidate, included so the release report is
one artifact.

oneOf.description: Worst severity present (absent for an empty diff).

SendWindow.description:
Time window during which a step is allowed to execute.
Hours are in 24h format relative to the instance's timezone.

days.description: Days of week allowed (0=Mon .. 6=Sun). Empty means all days.

$schema.description: Editor-facing JSON Schema link. It is metadata and does not affect execution.

deprecated.description:
If true, this version is deprecated. New instances should use a newer version.
Running instances bound to this version continue unaffected.

input_schema.description:
Optional JSON Schema validated against `context.data` at instance
create. When present, a create whose data fails validation is
rejected (HTTP 422) before the instance is persisted. Doubles as the
contract the dashboard renders an input form from.

oneOf.description: Lifecycle interceptors (before/after step, on-signal, on-complete, on-failure).

on_cancel.description:
Best-effort cleanup blocks run when the instance reaches terminal
`Cancelled`. Same semantics as `on_failure`.

on_failure.description:
Best-effort cleanup blocks run when the instance reaches terminal
`Failed`. Each top-level step block is dispatched once; errors are
swallowed (the instance is already failing). Use to release resources,
send a death notification, etc. — so a failed run doesn't "just die".

oneOf.description:
Alert-only SLA policy. When set, an instance exceeding `max_runtime`
(or a step exceeding `max_step_runtime`) emits an `instance.sla_breached`
webhook and increments `orch8_sla_breached_total` — the instance is NOT
failed or paused.

SequenceStatus.description: Lifecycle status for sequences: Draft → Staging → Production → Unpublished.

Session.description: A session groups related instances and holds shared data across them.

data.description: Session-scoped shared data accessible by all instances in this session.

expires_at.description: Optional TTL — session expires after this time.

secret.description: Optional HMAC secret for signing pushed envelopes.

SlaPolicy.description:
Alert-only service-level-agreement policy for a sequence. A breach is a
signal, not a state change: it fires one webhook + metric per breach kind
and leaves the instance running. Both bounds are optional.

max_runtime.description:
Maximum wall-clock lifetime of an instance, measured from `created_at`.
One `max_runtime` alert per instance.

max_step_runtime.description:
Maximum wall-clock time the current step may stay running/waiting,
measured from when it started. One alert per breaching step.

depends_on.description:
Effect blocks that must be compensated after this block. The planner
reverses these forward dependencies deterministically.

cache_key.description:
If set, cache step output under this key in the instance KV state.
On subsequent executions, if a cached value exists for the resolved key,
the handler is skipped and the cached value is returned directly.
The key is template-resolved before lookup (e.g. `"rate_{{ data.currency }}"`).

cancellable.description:
If false, this step will not be cancelled when the instance receives a cancel signal.
Used for cleanup/finalization steps that must complete.

oneOf.description: Receipt-backed recovery action for this externally visible step.
Restrict which context sections this step can access. If omitted, all sections visible.

deadline.description:
SLA deadline: maximum wall-clock time from when this step starts running.
If breached, the escalation handler is invoked and the step is failed.

fallback_handler.description:
Fallback handler to invoke when the primary handler's circuit breaker
is `Open`. When set, step dispatch re-targets to this handler instead
of deferring the instance for the cooldown window; when unset, the
legacy behaviour applies (defer to `now + remaining_cooldown_secs`).
Uses the same params + context as the primary handler; its own
failures are tracked under its own breaker key.

oneOf.description:
Handler to invoke when the SLA deadline is breached.
If omitted but deadline is set, the step simply fails on breach.

output_schema.description:
Optional JSON Schema that the handler output must conform to.
Validated after handler returns; schema violation is a permanent failure.

queue_name.description:
Named task queue for routing to dedicated worker pools.
If omitted, uses the default queue.

rate_limit_key.description: If set, this step consumes a rate limit token for the given resource key.

oneOf.description: If set, only execute during the specified time window (per instance timezone).

If set, this step pauses execution and waits for human input via a signal.
The signal name is `human_input:{block_id}`. Contains optional timeout.

when.description:
Conditional guard expression. When set, the step is only executed if the
expression evaluates to a truthy value; otherwise the step is skipped
(marked `NodeState::Skipped`). Uses the same expression syntax as router
conditions — `data.*`, `outputs.*`, comparisons, boolean ops.

StepLog.description: A stored step log line, annotated with the block it belongs to.

StepLogEntry.description: One log line captured during (or reported for) a step's execution.

SubSequenceDef.description:
Invoke another sequence as a child workflow.
The child instance is created and linked; the parent waits for completion.

input.description: Input data to pass as the child instance's initial context data.

sequence_name.description: Name of the sequence to invoke (resolved by tenant + namespace + name).

version.description: Optional specific version. If omitted, uses the latest non-deprecated version.

oneOf.description: Optional resource budget enforced by the scheduler (see [`Budget`]).

concurrency_key.description: Optional concurrency key for limiting parallel executions.

idempotency_key.description: Optional idempotency key for deduplication at creation time.

max_concurrency.description: Max concurrent running instances with the same concurrency key.

oneOf.description: Parent instance ID (set when this instance is a sub-sequence child).

session_id.description: Session ID for cross-instance shared state.

TimelineEntry.description:
One executed-block entry: the persisted snapshot of a single block
execution (first attempt, retry marker, loop iteration, ...).

completed_at.description:
When this row was persisted — i.e. when the block's execution (or the
sentinel write) completed.

is_sentinel.description:
`true` for internal bookkeeping rows (crash-recovery sentinels, retry
markers, error markers) — flagged rather than hidden.

output.description:
Inline output payload. Omitted when `include_outputs=false`. For
artifact-backed (externalized) rows the stored reference marker is
returned as-is — resolve via `output_ref`.

output_ref.description:
Externalized-payload reference, or a sentinel tag
(`__in_progress__` / `__retry__` / `__error__`).

oneOf.description:
Current execution context. Omitted when `include_outputs=false`
(contexts can be as large as outputs).

entries.description:
Executed-block entries in execution order (`created_at ASC`),
paginated by `offset` / `limit`.

state_transitions.description:
State transitions recorded in the audit log (chronological, capped at
the most recent 200). Empty when audit logging is not enabled.

TimelineStateTransition.description: A recorded instance state transition (from the audit log).

TriggerDef.description: A persisted trigger definition that maps an event source to a sequence.

secret.description:
Optional secret for HMAC validation of incoming requests.
Redacted in Debug/Serialize output — use `.secret.as_ref().map(|s| s.expose())` to access.

sequence_name.description: Sequence name to instantiate when fired.

slug.description: Unique slug used in the trigger URL / identifier.

version.description: Optional specific version. If omitted, uses latest.

TriggerPollState.description:
Runtime state for a polling trigger (`TriggerType::ActivepiecesPoll`).

Stored separately from [`TriggerDef`] so the poll loop can persist its
cursor and failure bookkeeping without rewriting the user-authored
trigger definition (avoiding lost-update races with API edits).

consecutive_failures.description: Number of consecutive failed polls. Reset to 0 on success.

last_error.description: Error message from the most recent failed poll. Cleared on success.

last_poll_at.description: When the last poll attempt (success or failure) completed.

slug.description: Slug of the trigger this state belongs to.

state.description:
Opaque cursor blob returned by the sidecar's last successful poll
(`ActivePieces` store contents — `lastPoll` epoch, item ids, ...).
Sent back verbatim on the next poll for deduplication.

TriggerType.description: The kind of event source that fires a trigger.

TrustBoundaryProfile.description:
Opinionated profiles make the highest-value trust-boundary use cases
deployable without inventing policy from scratch.

value.description: When set, replaces the stored secret. Write-only — never returned.

sample.description: How many historical instances to replay (default 10, max 50).

skip.description: Skip replay entirely (draft → ready with an audit record).

inconclusive.description:
Runs that could not be judged because recorded outputs were
missing — never silently treated as success.

matches.description: Runs whose path and terminal state matched the recording.

VariantStats.description: Aggregated terminal counts for one variant during canary.

WebhookDeliveryAttempt.description:
One delivery attempt (bounded, redacted metadata only — never the
payload or response body).

delivery_id.description:
Groups the attempts of one delivery pass (initial emit or one
redelivery).

error_excerpt.description:
Bounded, redacted excerpt of the transport error (never a response
body).

WebhookDeliverySummary.description: Aggregated view of one delivery (all attempts in a group).

oneOf.description: Error class of the final attempt when the delivery failed.

WebhookOutboxEntry.description:
One outbound webhook delivery. `Pending`/`InFlight` rows are being worked
by the engine; `Parked` rows failed after all retries and were kept for
manual inspection / redelivery.

attempts.description: How many delivery attempts were made so far.

claimed_at.description:
When an `InFlight` row was claimed; stale claims older than the
dispatcher's worst-case retry pass are recovered back to `Pending`.

created_at.description: When the delivery was first enqueued (or parked, for pre-drain rows).

delivery_id.description:
Links this entry to its attempt history (see
`webhook_delivery::WebhookDeliveryAttempt`). `None` for rows parked
before attempt tracking existed.

instance_id.description: The related instance id, if the event carried one.

last_error.description: The last error (HTTP status or transport error) seen, if any.

next_attempt_at.description:
When a `Pending` row becomes due for its next dispatch attempt.
`None` means immediately due (fresh rows) or not scheduled (`Parked`).

payload.description: The full serialized `WebhookEvent` payload, replayed verbatim on redelivery.

url.description: The destination URL the delivery was targeting.

WebhookOutboxStatus.description:
Delivery lifecycle of an outbox row.

`Pending` rows are due for dispatch (the drain loop or the in-memory fast
path claims them); `InFlight` rows are claimed by a dispatcher right now
(a stale claim is reset to `Pending` if the dispatcher dies mid-dispatch);
`Parked` rows exhausted their retries and await manual redelivery — the
drain loop never touches them.

WorkbenchEvent.description:
One event on the unified timeline. Ordering contract: `(timestamp,
kind, id)` — equal timestamps order by kind (state transitions before
outputs before logs), then by id, so repeated queries render
identically.

WorkerAttemptEventKind.description: Durable reason for a worker-task attempt transition.

WorkerCommand.description:
A control command queued for a specific worker, delivered via the worker
control channel (`GET /workers/{id}/commands`). The worker acts on pending
commands and acks them (`DELETE /workers/commands/{id}`).

command.description:
`drain` (stop claiming new tasks, finish in-flight), `reload`
(re-read config / re-register handlers), `ping` (liveness probe), or
`place` (accept a placement payload for runtime-local execution).

payload.description: Optional command parameters (e.g. a drain deadline).

WorkerInfo.description:
Aggregated view of one worker on the fleet, grouped from its
per-handler registrations.

alive.description: True when the worker polled within the liveness window.

handlers.description: Handler names this worker has polled for.

in_flight.description: Number of tasks currently claimed by this worker.

queues.description: Named queues this worker has polled (empty when default queue only).

version.description: Most recently reported version string, if any.

WorkerRegistration.description:
A worker's self-reported registration, refreshed on every poll.

One row per `(worker_id, handler_name)` pair — a worker that serves three
handlers appears three times. `last_seen_at` is bumped on every poll, so
liveness is "polled recently", independent of whether tasks were claimed.

queue_name.description: Named queue the worker polled, when using queue-scoped polling.

tenant_id.description: Tenant scope of the polling credential, when tenant-scoped.

WorkerTask.description: A task dispatched to an external worker for execution.

claim_epoch.description:
Monotonic ownership generation. Every successful claim increments this
value. Workers must echo it on every lease mutation so a process from an
older claim cannot act after the task has been reclaimed, even when the
same stable `worker_id` is reused.

context.description: Serialized `ExecutionContext` — kept as raw JSON to avoid coupling workers to Rust types.

queue_name.description: Named task queue for routing to dedicated worker pools.

requirements.description:
Capability, locality, and trust facts a runtime must satisfy before it
can atomically claim this task.

resume_checkpoint.description:
Latest durable progress snapshot supplied by the activity worker.
A replacement worker receives this value when it claims the task.

WorkerTaskAttemptEvent.description: Append-only evidence for one transition of one worker claim generation.

WorkerTaskState.description: State of a worker task in its lifecycle.

WorkerVersionPin.description:
A minimum-worker-version pin for a `(tenant, handler)` pair. A worker
reporting a version below `min_version` is not given tasks for that handler
at poll time — used to roll a fixed worker build out before old workers can
pick up affected work.

canary_percent.description:
Percentage of new instances routed to the candidate during
canary (0–100).

canary_started_at.description: When the canary started (observation window lower bound).

sequence_name.description:
Display name (the sequence name at creation) — informational
only; routing always uses the exact ids below.

validation_summary.description: Result summary of the last historical validation run, if any.

tags.description: Shared secrets referenced by step params via credentials://<id>

tags.description: Trigger definitions that convert inbound events into instance creations
